methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
DroneForge is a Pre-Seed stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Chester Zelaya, having raised $2.5M to date. The broader sector comprises five private peer companies (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, Elroy Air) and no public comparables, limiting peer-based valuation depth.

Given data constraints, Stage-Progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total raised ($2.5M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Pre-Seed to next-stage multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $6.25M. Peer-Median methodology is not viable; while five same-sector peers exist, none meet filters for stage proximity, adjacent-stage comparability, or similar valuation tier—a minimum of three datapoints is required to establish meaningful median benchmarks.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.3M to $7.2M, with a median point of $6M. Key uncertainties include the absence of early-stage peer valuations in the Drones & Autonomous space that would anchor relative valuation, product traction and go-to-market milestones post-seed, and capital efficiency relative to sector peers. A fuller assessment would benefit from downstream comparable transaction data or greater transparency into peer funding rounds at equivalent stages.
